Filter Outlier Samples Based on Protein Counts

filter_outlier_samples.Rd

This function identifies and removes entire samples that are considered outliers based on the total number of non-missing proteins identified within them.

The method calculates the mean and standard deviation of protein counts across all samples. A sample is flagged as an outlier if its total protein count falls outside the range defined by a specified number of standard deviations (sds) from the mean.

Usage

filter_outlier_samples(object, sds = 3)

Arguments

object

A ProtData object.

sds

The number of standard deviations from the mean protein count to use as the outlier threshold. Defaults to 3.

Value

A ProtData object with the outlier samples removed from the data and condition slots.

Examples

# Create data where one sample has a very low number of identified proteins
raw_data <- data.frame(
  Gene = c("GENEA", "GENEB", "GENEC", "GENED"),
  SampleA = c(10, 11, 12, 13),
  SampleB = c(12, 13, 14, 15),
  SampleC = c(11, 12, 13, 14),
  SampleD_outlier = c(NA, NA, NA, 5) # Only one protein found
)

pd_obj <- create_protdata(dat = raw_data)
cat("Dimensions before removing outliers:", dim(pd_obj@data), "\n")
#> Dimensions before removing outliers: 4 4 

# With sds=1, the outlier sample should be identified and removed.
filtered_obj <- remove_outliers(pd_obj, sds = 1)
#> Error in remove_outliers(pd_obj, sds = 1): could not find function "remove_outliers"
cat("Dimensions after removing outliers:", dim(filtered_obj@data), "\n")
#> Error: object 'filtered_obj' not found
print(colnames(filtered_obj@data))
#> Error: object 'filtered_obj' not found
